correctness.rationale: Every degree-at-most-two graph decomposes into cycles and paths. Saturated cycles force free amalgamation. Distinct cycle completions of any deficient path or isolate cannot amalgamate, establishing the exact AP bases. Old degree deficit 2(k+i) and at most two old neighbors per new vertex prove the universal vertex lower bound; a single isolate requires two new vertices. A cyclic bridge construction realizes each lower bound. At equality every labelled new vertex has exactly two distinct old neighbors, proving the exact coefficient formula without missing or double-counted graphs. A standalone brute-force checker verified all possible minimal completions for nine small component profiles.

value.rationale: Cofinal amalgamation naturally asks exactly which finite members support amalgamation and how to extend arbitrary members to one. The result gives a complete degree-two classification, a sharp nontrivial vertex-addition invariant and a fixed-labelled coefficient enumeration of all minima, plus an explicit computably categorical cofinal limit. Those exact structural and enumerative data are not a relabelling of a single generic CAP theorem.
